newsitem.title: New Zealand: Lower NZD, interest rates hoist NZ shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Lower NZD, interest rates hoist NZ shares at close.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end with slight gain
* Lower NZ dollar, interest rates, assist equities
* Lower Kiwi gives Air NZ "B" shares a boost
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +11.42 at 2,277.53

New Zealand share prices, assisted by a market-led easing of monetary conditions, ended with a modest gain on Friday but off their session highs.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 11.42 points higher at 2,277.53 against the day's high of 2,286.53.
Turnover totalled NZ$57.3 million.

Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said the rally in interest rate markets and the lower New Zealand dollar facilitated the gain, but nerves ahead of key U.S. wage and payrolls data saw the index retrace from its peak.

"This week has had a better tone to it than the two previous weeks," Koller said. "If we do get an endorsement of the easing so far by the Reserve Bank and if they were to surmise that it could go further, then certainly that is going to give our equities a boost."
Air New Zealand "B" shares got a shot in the arm from the lower Kiwi, finishing three cents higher at NZ$4.20 on high turnover.
All the Fletcher divisional shares gained and Telecom firmed three to $6.53.
Likewise Lion Nathan shrugged off Monday's poor interim result to end seven cents stronger at $3.57.
DB Group had a strong run, gaining 12 cents to $2.40, or an equivalent of $1.05 before its capital reduction, which became effective on Monday.
In retailing, Hallenstein Glasson gained 11 to NZ$2.12. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
